newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends weaker on commercial/fund selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends weaker on commercial/fund selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended weaker on Monday burdened by some commercial and fund selling as well as hedge pressure despite strength in the CBOT soy complex.

"We did see good commercial buying earlier in the session and saw commercial short covering at the close," a trader said. He noted traders were squaring up their positions ahead of Tuesday's production estimate issued by Statistics Canada.
November canola lost $1.80 at $424.40 and October flax fell $1.50 to $401.00.
But flax settled mixed in dull trading. The trader pointed to very light hedges and two-way commercial trade.

Feed wheat futures firmed except for spot October which dropped the $7.50 limit to $171.50. October was down on long liquidation and the lack of any front-end cash demand, another trader said. "The shorts are being patient, waiting for lower levels, but some commission house short covering was evident from December onward," he said.

Barley ended firmer amid a lack of significant hedge pressure. "Local short covering and commission house buying supported prices. November western barley was up $1.00 at $146.60. Feed peas did not open.
(All values in Canadian dollars except for feed peas and oats which are in U.S. dollars).
